markdown_report:
The next experiment should test **recent-context augmentation within one BERT4Rec model**, keeping supervision weights fixed.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Endpoint reconstruction matches appended-mask inference because neither has right context. Explicit weighting remains useful only when it differs algebraically from the baseline objective. (2) Electronics has a measured negative-beats-positive rate of 13.6%. This identifies a training-diagnostic weakness, but does not establish its cause or predict validation HR@10. (3) Qualitative feedback favors direct recent-interest connections over broad historical resemblance. Histories can support recency experiments, while ownership, compatibility and current demand remain unobserved.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [BERT4Rec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) already includes endpoint masking. Its contribution supports inference-aligned supervision, without making endpoint masking a new mechanism. (2) [Does It Look Sequential?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008) motivates testing whether history order matters. Its findings do not establish that these four datasets require stronger recency. (3) [Hidasi and Czapp](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/eval_flaws_recsys23.pdf) show that sampled evaluation can change model ordering. Therefore, auxiliary probes must remain separate from the pinned selection metric.

**Framework.** Three directions separate intervention from evidence:

| Direction | Minimal intervention | Evidence and remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision allocation | Endpoint weight 0.75 | Tests allocation; cannot isolate context mismatch |
| Context availability | Randomly shorten endpoint history | Tests recent-context training; may discard useful interests |
| Behavioral diagnosis | Matched recent/older removals | Measures sensitivity; cannot verify current intent |

**Candidate assessments.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Endpoint weight 0.75 — 2/5/3.** Originality: explicit control is useful, but weighting is established. Potential: inexpensive allocation evidence, but heuristic. Difficulty: a small loss edit, but exact reductions require care.
- **Recent-context augmentation — 4/6/3.** Originality: connects endpoint supervision with context-length variation, but cropping is established. Potential: tests robustness to stale history, but may favor short-term popularity. Difficulty: a sampler edit, but matched construction is essential.
- **Matched history-removal probe — 3/6/4.** Originality: controlled comparison clarifies sensitivity, but perturbation methods exist. Potential: informs later interventions, but supplies no direct accuracy improvement. Difficulty: reuses inference, but positional controls require care.

**Selected experiment.** At 10% progress, choose recent-context augmentation. For endpoint examples only, retain the latest ten preceding interactions with probability 0.25; otherwise retain baseline context. Preserve reconstruction examples, loss reductions and group weights. Compare against the exact corrected baseline using matched target draws and update counts.

```python
context, target = baseline_endpoint_draw()
if augmentation_rng.random() < 0.25:
    context = context[-10:]
sequence = left_pad(context[-(L-1):] + [MASK], L)
loss = unchanged_baseline_objective(sequence, target, reconstruction_group)
```

Keep ordinary inference unchanged, all four categories, fixed seeds and training limits. Preserve diagnostic interfaces and predictor consistency. Select solely by host macro validation HR@10 within the shared budget; no improvement is presently established.

idea.description: Test randomized recent-context augmentation for endpoint supervision within each category’s single corrected BERT4Rec model. With probability 0.25, retain only the latest ten observed interactions preceding an endpoint target; otherwise retain the baseline context. Keep reconstruction supervision and objective weights unchanged.
idea.motivation: The qualitative diagnosis suggests that broad historical associations sometimes outrank direct recent-interest connections. Shortened endpoint contexts offer a small, testable training intervention using observed histories, without claiming that recency reveals current demand. This differs from the prior weight-only proposals by changing available context while holding supervision allocation fixed.
idea.implementation_notes: Use the supplied corrected baseline as the exact control; its source is not included here, so this is an implementation specification rather than a drop-in train.py. Apply cropping only to explicitly generated endpoint examples, identified by provenance. If the baseline lacks that group, introducing it requires a matched-construction control; do not attribute such a combined change to cropping alone. Omit the experiment if all eligible contexts already contain ten or fewer interactions. Preserve target draws, reconstruction masks, group membership, loss denominators, group weights, optimizer and update counts across arms. Use a separate deterministic augmentation RNG derived from training seed 42 so cropping does not perturb other sampling streams. Reserve one input position for MASK and keep every supervised occurrence masked. Retained training items should occupy the same right-aligned positions as in the corresponding baseline endpoint input. Do not change timestamps or splits. Inference retains the baseline full allowed history, appends MASK, left-pads and reads the actual final nonpadding position, never count-1. Keep one independently trained checkpoint per category, all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch, and single-GPU execution. Preserve the predictor writer and ModelView interfaces. DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) must continue returning metrics and metric_definitions; diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) must use those measured values and definitions. Retain B x L diagnostic batches and measure only valid supervised MASK positions. Record cropping eligibility, realized crop rate and retained lengths. Select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10, charging training and diagnostics to the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. No independent predictors, checkpoint averaging, external weights or unavailable attributes are introduced.
idea.pseudocode:
spec = document_corrected_baseline()
assert experiment_is_not_a_noop(spec, recent_length=10)
plan = predeclare_exact_control_and_context_augmentation()
# Add a matched-construction control only if endpoint groups must be introduced.
# Reduce the comparison set if required controls exceed the shared budget.
for arm in plan:
    for category in four_categories:
        model = initialize_corrected_bert4rec(seed=42)
        sampling = reset_matched_baseline_sampling_stream(category)
        augmentation_rng = separate_deterministic_rng(seed=42)
        for epoch in range(max_epochs_at_most_200):
            for step in range(200):
                stop_if_predeclared_compute_allocation_exhausted()
                batch = sampling.draw_baseline_batch()
                if arm == 'context_augmentation':
                    for example in batch.explicit_endpoint_examples:
                        if augmentation_rng.random() < 0.25:
                            example.context = example.context[-10:]
                        example.input = left_pad(
                            example.context[-(L-1):] + [MASK], L)
                assert_supervised_inputs_are_reserved_MASK(batch)
                loss = spec.unchanged_objective(model, batch)
                optimizer.zero_grad()
                loss.backward()
                optimizer.step()
                record_realized_context_lengths_and_compute()
        save_one_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor(model, category)
# Compare with the unchanged host macro validation HR@10.
# Freeze the selected configuration before held-out inference.
# Deploy exactly one trained checkpoint per category.

originality.positive: Connects endpoint supervision and randomized context availability in a controlled response to the supplied qualitative diagnosis.
originality.negative: History cropping and context augmentation are established techniques; this is a task-specific hypothesis rather than a new backbone or masking principle.

future_potential.positive: A controlled result could motivate research on which history horizons support endpoint prediction while retaining one shared encoder.
future_potential.negative: Cropping can discard persistent interests, and any validation gain would not establish improved compatibility, current demand or the proposed mechanism.

code_difficulty.positive: Primarily changes endpoint input construction and leaves model architecture and deployed scoring unchanged.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact baseline preservation, deterministic sampling, position alignment and missing endpoint-group controls require careful integration.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Uses bidirectional masked-item reconstruction and appended-mask next-item prediction.
Includes endpoint masking, providing the established supervision setting for the proposed context intervention.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed cropping probability or history length improves this benchmark.
Interior reconstruction and endpoint inference have different available contexts.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Examines history-order dependence across sequential recommendation datasets.
Motivates checking behavioral sensitivity before interpreting a sequential model’s predictions.
limitations: Order perturbations do not verify current user intent.
Its findings do not determine the best context horizon for these four datasets.

related_work.title: The Effect of Sampling on Evaluation of Recommender Systems
contributions: Documents evaluation distortions and model-order changes associated with candidate sampling.
limitations: Provides evaluation guidance rather than an endpoint-training algorithm.
Does not justify modifying the pinned host evaluator.
